evidence: Home page shows 6 template cards, each with title, author (e.g. "Sarah Chen"), and description (e.g. "A clean, modern resume template...").
Each card shows title, author, description, category badge, scenario badge, usage count (e.g. "1,250 uses"), and update date (e.g. "Updated 2024-12-01").
Clicking "Use Template" on Professional Resume opened a preview panel with title "Professional Resume", Fill Template/Preview Result tabs, and a form listing all 14 template fields.

With fields empty, preview.missing-fields shows "Required fields missing Please fill in: Full Name, Job Title, Email, Professional Summary, ..." and the Preview Result tab is disabled (click timed out: 'element is not enabled').
Preview Result tab is disabled while required fields are unfilled, confirmed by click timeout showing element not enabled.

All 14 fields of the Professional Resume template (name, title, email, phone, summary, company, position, startDate, endDate, responsibilities, degree, school, graduationYear, skills) accepted typed values via browser_fill_form.

After filling all required fields, Preview Result tab became enabled and rendered a document with entered values substituted (name, title, summary, company, position, dates, degree, school, skills all present in preview.result).

Clipboard content for Professional Resume (a Markdown template) after filling: '# Timothee Issenmann

**Software Engineer** | ... | 

---

## Professional Summary
...' - shows H1/H2/H3 headings, bold emphasis, --- separator, and line breaks all rendered correctly, with every placeholder replaced by entered values and no unresolved placeholders.
Clicking "Copy to Clipboard" changed button label to "Copied!" (visible feedback) and navigator.clipboard.readText() returned the exact Markdown-formatted generated result.

actual: Email input has type=\"email\" but entering the invalid value \"not-an-email\" did not block the preview: Preview Result tab became enabled and the generated output included the literal invalid string \"not-an-email\" in place of a validated email address, with no error shown.

evidence: Markdown template (Professional Resume) rendered proper Markdown structure (headings, bold, separators) with field substitution; content matches expected Markdown output.

issue: Markdown control characters (*, #) in field values are not neutralized and alter generated formatting
actual: The app blocks < > { } [ ] \\ | ` with error "Special characters like < > { } [ ] \\ | ` are not allowed", but entering "# Fake Heading *Bold Injection*" as the Full Name value was accepted and rendered in the preview with the asterisk text parsed as actual Markdown emphasis (rendered as italic \"Bold Injection\" inside the H1), altering the generated document's formatting/structure instead of being shown as literal text.

evidence: Clicking the favorite toggle in the preview panel immediately set its state to "on", updated the header Favorites button label to "Favorites 1", and set the corresponding grid card's favorite state to "on".

Favorited two templates (Professional Resume, Weekly Status Report); header Favorites button showed count "2". Clicking header.favorites toggled favorites-only mode (state "on") and templates.grid narrowed to exactly the 2 favorited items ("Showing 2 of 6 templates").

While favorites-only mode was active, typing "weekly" into search narrowed the grid from 2 favorited templates down to 1 ("Weekly Status Report", "Showing 1 of 6 templates"), confirming search/filter work within the favorites-only view.

issue: "Oldest First" sort produces the same order as "Recently Updated"
actual: Category filter (Resume) correctly narrowed 6→1 templates; Scenario filter (Academic) correctly narrowed 6→1; Alphabetical sort correctly ordered titles A-Z. However, selecting "Oldest First" produced the exact same order (Professional Email, Professional Resume, Weekly Status Report, Meeting Minutes, Project Proposal, Academic Research Summary) as selecting "Recently Updated" (newest), reproduced twice. Oldest-first should reverse/differ from newest-first ordering.

evidence: Category filter, scenario filter, favorites-only toggle, and sort selections all updated filters.result-count and templates.grid content immediately in the same page session without any navigation/reload calls.

Typing "res" (3 chars) showed real-time suggestions (Professional Resume, Responsibilities, In Progress, Academic Research Summary, Research Title). Clicking "Professional Resume" suggestion filled the search box with "Professional Resume" and narrowed the grid to 1 matching template.

actual: Searching "Resme" (missing letter) and "Reusme" (transposed letters), both minor typos of "Resume", returned "Showing 0 of 6 templates" with "No templates found" and no suggestions offered, instead of matching/suggesting the "Professional Resume" template.

issue: Custom template submitted despite field/placeholder mismatch; preview contains unresolved placeholders
actual: Submitted a custom template with content "Hello {{userName}}, welcome to {{companyName}}!" but only declared one field (label "userName"); submission succeeded (template count went from 6 to 7) despite {{companyName}} having no matching field. When used, even the filled field failed to substitute due to a key-casing mismatch (field key "username" vs placeholder "{{userName}}"), and the generated preview literally contained "Greeting Hello {{userName}}, welcome to {{companyName}}!" with both placeholders unresolved.

issue: Duplicate field labels are accepted, not rejected or disambiguated
actual: Added a field labeled "recipientName", then added a second field with the identical label "recipientName". Both were accepted into the field list with the same generated id/placeholder key "{{recipientname}}", no warning or rejection was shown, and the Submit Template button remained enabled/active.

evidence: Successfully submitted custom templates via the Submit Template dialog with title, description, author, category, scenario, Markdown/plain-text content, and at least one defined field each time (e.g. "Simple Greeting Note", "Isolated Test Template"). Submission succeeded and dialog closed.

After submitting "Isolated Test Template" (content "Message: {{message}}", field "message"), it appeared in templates.grid (count 8→9), was selectable via Use Template, its form field was fillable, and the generated preview correctly showed "Message: Hello World" with the placeholder substituted.

Submitting each custom template immediately updated filters.result-count (e.g. "Showing 7 of 7" → "Showing 8 of 8" → "Showing 9 of 9") and templates.grid content without any page navigation/reload call.

Clicking Submit Template with all fields (title, author, description, content) blank and no fields defined kept the dialog open and did not add a new template (grid count stayed at 6), confirming blank required fields block submission.

After navigating to reload the app, header.favorites.count still showed "2" (favorites preserved), and all 3 custom templates submitted earlier (Isolated Test Template, Simple Greeting Note, QA Test Template) remained in templates.grid, with "Showing 9 of 9 templates".
